subject: English
prompt: Choose the correct article: He is ___ honorary member of the club.
explain: 'Honorary' begins with a silent h, so it starts with a vowel sound: an.

subject: English
prompt: Choose the correct article: The driver took ___ U-turn at the signal.
explain: 'U' is pronounced 'yoo', which starts with the consonant sound /j/: a U-turn.

subject: English
prompt: Choose the correct article: She is pursuing ___ MBA from Pilani.
explain: 'M' is pronounced 'em', a vowel sound, so it takes an.

subject: English
prompt: Choose the correct article: He is ___ one-eyed man.
explain: 'One' begins with the consonant sound /w/, so it takes a.

subject: English
prompt: Choose the correct article: She is ___ European diplomat.
explain: 'European' starts with the /j/ sound, which is a consonant sound: a.

subject: English
prompt: Choose the correct article: The doctor advised ___ X-ray of the chest.
explain: 'X' is pronounced 'eks', a vowel sound, so it takes an.

subject: English
prompt: Choose the correct article: He is ___ 8-year-old boy.
explain: 'Eight' starts with a vowel sound, so it takes an, even though it is written as a numeral.

subject: English
prompt: Choose the correct article: She works as ___ UNESCO consultant.
explain: UNESCO is pronounced 'yoo-NES-koh', so it starts with the /j/ sound: a.

subject: English
prompt: Of the two sisters, Rina is ___ taller.
explain: 'Of the two' makes the comparative specific, so 'the taller' is used.

subject: English
prompt: Fill in: ___ Earth revolves around ___ Sun.
explain: Unique, one-of-a-kind objects take 'the'.

subject: English
prompt: Which name correctly takes 'the' before it?
explain: Mountain ranges (the Himalayas) take 'the'; single peaks and lakes do not.

subject: English
prompt: I bought a shirt and a tie. ___ shirt was blue.
explain: A noun mentioned a second time becomes specific, so 'the' is used.

subject: English
prompt: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: He studies the English at school.
The French are known for their cuisine.
explain: 'The' + nationality adjective names a people. Languages and countries take no 'the'.

subject: English
prompt: ___ more you read, ___ more you learn.
explain: 'The … the …' is the fixed structure for paired comparatives.

subject: English
prompt: She plays ___ sitar very well.
explain: 'The' is used before the name of a musical instrument when we speak of playing it.

subject: English
prompt: ___ rich should help ___ poor.
explain: 'The' + adjective denotes a whole class of people.

subject: English
prompt: This is ___ very book I was looking for.
explain: 'The' goes with 'very', 'same' and 'only' to point to one specific thing.

subject: English
prompt: Fill in the blank: ___ honey is rich in natural sugars.
explain: An uncountable noun used generically takes no article.

subject: English
prompt: Fill in the blank: ___ honesty is the best policy.
explain: A generic abstract noun takes zero article.

subject: English
prompt: Which sentence speaks of cars in general?
options: The cars in that showroom are costly.
The cars I bought are red.
explain: A bare plural noun is generic; the others are specific.

subject: English
prompt: Spot the error: "She gave me an advice on health." Best correction?
explain: Advice is uncountable and takes no a/an; use "a piece of advice" if needed.

subject: English
prompt: Fill in the blank: ___ water in this tank is unsafe to drink.
explain: A specific, particular water (in this tank) takes "the", not zero article.

subject: English
prompt: Fill in the blank: Children need ___ love and care to grow well.
explain: Uncountable abstract nouns used in a general sense take zero article.

subject: English
prompt: Fill in the blank: ___ music of Ravi Shankar is soothing.
explain: An of-phrase makes the noun specific, so "the" is needed.

subject: English
prompt: Which nouns take the zero article when used in a general sense?
explain: Generic plural countable and uncountable nouns have no article.

subject: English
prompt: Choose the correct option: Delhi is ___ most polluted city in northern India.
explain: A superlative adjective compared within a group takes 'the'.

subject: English
prompt: Pick the correct sentence.
options: She is my the best friend.
She is the my best friend.
explain: A possessive and 'the' never stand together; 'my best friend' is correct.

subject: English
prompt: In 'He is a most generous man', what does 'a most' mean?
explain: 'A most' (not 'the most') gives the sense of 'very', with no comparison.

subject: English
prompt: Fill in: ___ equator divides the earth into two hemispheres.
explain: Unique, one-of-a-kind things (the equator, the sun, the sky) take 'the'.

subject: English
prompt: Fill in: Gandhi ji was ___ first Indian to be called 'Father of the Nation'.
explain: Ordinals such as first and second, like superlatives, take 'the'.

subject: English
topic: Articles with proper nouns & geographic names
prompt: Which of these geographic names is used WITHOUT the article 'the'?
explain: Single lakes take no article; ranges, seas and rivers take 'the'.

subject: English
topic: Articles with proper nouns & geographic names
prompt: Fill in: '___ Alps are in Europe, and ___ Mont Blanc is their highest peak.'
explain: Mountain ranges take 'the'; a single peak takes no article.

subject: English
topic: Articles with proper nouns & geographic names
prompt: Which island name normally takes 'the'?
explain: Island groups take 'the' (the Maldives); single islands do not.

subject: English
topic: Articles with proper nouns & geographic names
prompt: Which country name takes 'the' before it?
explain: Plural-form country names take 'the': the Netherlands, the Philippines.

subject: English
topic: Articles with proper nouns & geographic names
prompt: Fill in: '___ Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world.'
explain: Names of deserts take 'the': the Sahara, the Thar.

subject: English
topic: Articles with proper nouns & geographic names
prompt: Fill in: '___ Mr. Verma is waiting outside' (a stranger named Verma).
explain: 'A' before a proper name means 'a certain person called'.

subject: English
topic: Omission of articles: meals, games, languages
prompt: Fill in the blank: "Have you had ___ breakfast yet?"
explain: Meal names used in a general sense take no article.

subject: English
topic: Omission of articles: meals, games, languages
prompt: Fill in the blank: "Mother prepared ___ excellent lunch for the guests."
explain: A meal modified by an adjective takes an article; 'excellent' starts with a vowel sound, so 'an'.

subject: English
topic: Omission of articles: meals, games, languages
prompt: Fill in the blank: "___ dinner you cooked yesterday was delicious."
explain: A specific, defined meal (the one you cooked) takes 'the'.

subject: English
topic: Omission of articles: meals, games, languages
prompt: Which sentence is correct?
explain: Names of games take no article.

subject: English
topic: Omission of articles: meals, games, languages
prompt: Which is correct? "My brother is very fond of ___ chess."
explain: Games like chess, cricket and tennis are used without articles.

subject: English
topic: Omission of articles: meals, games, languages
prompt: In "The French are known for their cuisine", 'The French' means:
explain: 'The' + nationality adjective refers to the people of that nation.

subject: English
topic: Omission of articles: meals, games, languages
prompt: Fill in the blank: "I am learning ___ Spanish language."
explain: A language name alone has no article, but with the word 'language' it takes 'the'.

subject: English
prompt: Choose the correct sentence: The patient was taken to ___ hospital and admitted at once.
formula: Institution used for its purpose → no article
explain: Hospital as a place of treatment (its purpose) takes no article in American/standard exam usage? Use: British 'in hospital' = as patient.

subject: English
prompt: The parents went to ___ school to meet the principal about the fee issue.
explain: Visiting the building, not for studying, takes 'the'; 'go to school' (as students) takes none.

subject: English
prompt: The thief was sent to ___ jail for two years.
formula: go to jail = as an inmate (no article)
explain: Institution used for its main purpose (imprisonment) takes zero article, like school, church, hospital.

subject: English
prompt: Choose the correct word: "___ kind of book bores me."
explain: 'Kind' is singular, so it takes 'this/that' with a singular noun (this kind of book).

subject: English
prompt: Fill in: "The roads of Mumbai are wider than ___ of Pune."
explain: 'Those of' replaces the plural noun 'roads' and avoids repetition.

subject: English
prompt: Fill in: "___ who work hard seldom fail."
explain: 'Those who' is the standard phrase meaning 'people who'.

subject: English
prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
explain: 'News' is uncountable and singular, so it takes 'this' and 'is'.

subject: English
prompt: Choose the correct form: He gave me ___ during the interview.
explain: Advice is uncountable, so it takes 'much' and has no plural form.

subject: English
prompt: Fill in the blank: Would you like ___ coffee?
explain: 'Some' is used in offers and requests, even in questions.

subject: English
prompt: Fill in the blank: He has hardly ___ money left.
explain: 'Hardly' is negative in sense, so 'any' is used, not 'some'.

subject: English
prompt: In 'Any student can apply', the word 'any' means:
explain: In affirmative sentences, 'any' means 'no matter which' or 'whichever'.

subject: English
prompt: Fill in the blank: Too ___ cooks spoil the broth.
explain: 'Cooks' is a plural countable noun, so 'too many' is used.

subject: English
prompt: Fill in the blank: Much of ___ time was wasted.
explain: 'Much of' must be followed by a determiner or pronoun, such as 'the'.

subject: English
prompt: Fill in the blank: If you have ___ doubts, please ask me.
explain: 'Any' is used in if-clauses, questions and negatives.

subject: English
prompt: In 'Few people attended the meeting', what does 'few' convey?
explain: 'Few' (without 'a') means hardly any; it carries a negative sense.

subject: English
prompt: 'Not a few' mistakes were found in the report. 'Not a few' means:
formula: not a few = quite a number
explain: 'Not a few' is a negation of 'a few' and means a considerable number, i.e. many.

subject: English
prompt: Fill in: 'After the long walk, I felt ___ tired.'
explain: 'A little' used as an adverb before an adjective means 'somewhat'.

subject: English
prompt: In 'Little did he realise the danger', 'little' means:
explain: Sentence-initial adverb 'little' with inversion means 'not at all'.

subject: English
prompt: Spot the error: 'I have little books on this topic.'
explain: 'Books' is countable plural, so 'few' is needed instead of 'little'.

subject: English
prompt: Choose the correct verb: Every boy and every girl ___ invited to the party.
explain: Subjects joined by 'and' with 'every' each stay singular, so the verb is singular.

subject: English
prompt: Fill in the blank: Each of the players ___ a medal at the ceremony.
formula: each of + plural noun + singular verb
explain: 'Each' is singular, so it takes a singular verb even after 'of' + plural noun.

subject: English
prompt: Replace the word in capitals: 'NEITHER of the three boys passed.' Correct word?
explain: Neither/either refer to two only; for three or more, use 'none'.

subject: English
prompt: Neither the manager nor the clerks ___ aware of the change.
formula: neither…nor: verb agrees with the nearer subject
explain: The verb agrees with the nearer subject 'clerks', which is plural.

subject: English
prompt: Choose the correct form: Either of the two answers ___ acceptable.
explain: 'Either of' (two items) takes a singular verb in standard usage.

subject: English
prompt: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
options: Every of the students were rewarded.
Every one of the students was rewarded.
Every one of the students were rewarded.
Every of the students was rewarded.
explain: 'Every' cannot take 'of' directly; use 'every one of' + plural noun with a singular verb.

subject: English
prompt: Spot the error: 'Rita and her's brother went to a friend of ours.'
explain: Possessive pronoun 'hers' never takes an apostrophe; here 'her' (determiner) is needed before 'brother'.

subject: English
prompt: Choose the correct form: 'This book is not mine; ____ is on the shelf.'
formula: my + noun, but mine stands alone
explain: Mine is a possessive pronoun and stands alone; 'my' is a determiner needing a noun after it.

subject: English
prompt: Fill in the blank: 'She bought two ___ eggs for the cake.'
explain: After a definite number, 'dozen' stays singular; 'dozens of' is used without a number.

subject: English
prompt: Which determiner means 'some, though not many' with a positive sense?
explain: 'A few' means some, which is positive; 'few' means hardly any, which is negative.

subject: English
prompt: Fill in the blank: The ___ of students absent today was surprisingly high.
explain: 'Number' is used for countable nouns and 'amount' for uncountable ones.

subject: English
prompt: 'A great deal of' is followed by which kind of noun?
explain: 'A great deal of' is used only with uncountable nouns, e.g. a great deal of money.

subject: English
prompt: Reported speech: He said, "I like this book." → He said that he liked ___ book.
explain: In indirect speech the near demonstrative 'this' usually changes to 'that'.

subject: English
prompt: Fill in: 'There is ___ hope of his recovery; the doctors have given up.'
explain: Hope is uncountable, and 'little' has a negative sense (almost no hope).

subject: English
prompt: Which determiner can be used with both plural countable and uncountable nouns?
explain: 'Plenty of' (like 'a lot of') works with plural countable and uncountable nouns; many, several and few take only countable nouns.

subject: English
prompt: Which determiner cannot be used before an uncountable noun like 'rice'?
explain: 'Several' means more than two and goes only with plural countable nouns.
